Willie Clancy’s, X:6

Paddy O’Brien (Offaly) plays this in G mixolydian
(or dorian --the only B’s are in ornaments) in his Tune Collection.
He calls it “The Sweetafter”. He says that he heard it in a performance on RTE
television of Martin Hayes and Mary MacNamara when they were just teenagers
and that their music “touched the very soles of my feet”.

I know that those two got a lot of music from John Naughton, and this version
does sound like John Naughton’s way of concertina playing.
Paddy plays the tune single. I agree that the B-part is very like The Eel in the Sink.

↳ Posted by ithaca-markb on January 5th, 2026.

Re: Willie Clancy’s

Interesting Mark. I’ve played that John Naughton reel for many, many years. In fact, it’s one of my favourites but I never made the connection with this tune. Of course, I knew it had a B-part that crops up not just in The Eel in the Sink but also in several other reels including Scotch Mary and Molly Bán. The Naughton version of the A-part has such a different feel to it phrasing-wise that I never thought it might be based on this Willie Clancy tune. I see it now, though it’s still markedly it’s own buzz the way he played it.

Also, to reiterate my feelings regarding The Eel in the Sink, one should consider this very much a version of that tune, not just in the obvious B-part but also in the A part. If you play the A-part beginning on a higher octave E and change the mode to A mix you’ll see it immediately. I wouldn’t be inclined to play a long C sharp but something like this could work:

K: Amix
|eAAB cdec|dG G2 BGBd|eAAB cdef|gedg eAAd|

Re: Willie Clancy’s

Hey Paahto! I think we played some banjo tunes together at the Grady’s log house in Ithaca.
I’ve been busy transcribing all 1500 tunes from the three volumes of the Paddy O’Brien Tune Collection and they will soon all appear on the ITMA website.

I post some of them here, and was about to make a new tune posting for The Sweetafter in Gmix. But, first I searched for the tune. There was nothing similar in G, but I thought to transpose to A and search, and that brought me here.
It is clearly a version of the tune posted here, but does indeed have a different feel. But I don’t know if it deserves to be a separate tune or not.
